classification.difficultyReason: Uses the 3–4–5 trigonometric ratios, integrates the supplied velocity components, and applies Pythagoras and inverse tangent to explicitly requested position and velocity calculations.

content.prompt: A particle is projected from ground level with a speed of $60\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)$ to the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

answer.worked:
Integrating the velocity components,
$$\begin{align*}x&=36t+C_1,\\y&=-5t^2+48t+C_2.\end{align*}$$
At launch, $t=0$ and $x=y=0$, so $C_1=C_2=0$. Therefore
$$\begin{align*}x&=36t,\\y&=-5t^2+48t.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find, correct to one decimal place, the distance of the particle from the point of projection after $3$ seconds.

answer.worked:
At $t=3$,
$$\begin{align*}x(3)&=36(3)=108,\\y(3)&=-5(3)^2+48(3)\\&=-45+144\\&=99.\end{align*}$$
The distance from the point of projection is
$$\begin{align*}d&=\sqrt{108^2+99^2}\\&=\sqrt{21465}\\&\approx146.5\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Show that the velocity after $3$ seconds is $18\sqrt5\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right)$ above the horizontal.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\dot{x}(3)&=36,\\\dot{y}(3)&=-10(3)+48\\&=18.\end{align*}$$
Thus the speed is
$$\begin{align*}V&=\sqrt{36^2+18^2}\\&=\sqrt{1620}\\&=18\sqrt5\text{ m/s}.\end{align*}$$
Both velocity components are positive, so the direction is above the horizontal:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{18}{36}\right)\\&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac12\right).\end{align*}$$
